Thirteen methods call `async_op` directly. I found them by searching the workspace for `async_op(`, which turned up 13 call sites, and then matching each one to the function and `impl` block around it. Every call is written as `trace::async_op(...)`, inside a public `async fn` in the `tokio` crate. No other library crate calls it, and the test files only mention `async_op` in span names, not as a function call.

- **`tokio/src/time/interval.rs`:** `Interval::tick`
- **`tokio/src/sync/rwlock.rs`:** `RwLock::read`, `read_owned`, `write`, `write_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/semaphore.rs`:** `Semaphore::acquire`, `acquire_many`, `acquire_owned`, `acquire_many_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs`:** `Sender::closed`
- **`tokio/src/sync/barrier.rs`:** `Barrier::wait`
- **`tokio/src/sync/mutex.rs`:** `Mutex::lock`, `lock_owned`

Some files build the same tracing spans by hand instead of calling `async_op`, so they are not included. These are `Sleep` in `time/sleep.rs`, `Acquire::new` in `sync/batch_semaphore.rs`, and the oneshot `Receiver` setup in `sync/oneshot.rs`.
